fields.label: Call
fields.description: The call these artifacts belong to. It is also this row's NAME, so a lookup by call is a primary-key seek and one call can never grow two media rows.

fields.label: Transcript Source
fields.description: Who produced the text — the voice provider that ran the call, or a transcription service run over the recording afterwards.

fields.label: Summary
fields.description: The producer's own one-line account of the call, when it gives one. Absent is normal.

fields.label: Transcript
fields.description: The plain readable transcript. ALWAYS present whatever arrived — a reader never has to understand segments to read the call.

fields.label: Segments
fields.description: [{role?, start?, end?, text}] — ONE shape with optional parts. `role` is which SIDE of the call spoke (agent or contact), never a producer's own word for it and never a display label: what a screen calls each role is the screen's business. Plain text is segments with no role and no times; one producer gives role without times, another times without role, a third both. A new producer fills in fewer boxes, never a new shape.

fields.label: Raw Payload
fields.description: The producer's transcript payload, untouched. Kept deliberately: when a parser turns out wrong — and one will — this is what lets us re-derive instead of re-transcribing thousands of calls.

fields.label: Recording State
fields.description: Blank: nothing has been said about audio for this call yet. Awaiting: audio is expected and we do not hold it. Stored: the bytes are ours. Absent: the producer says this call has none. Abandoned: every retry was spent. The sweep's whole question is the Awaiting rows whose next attempt is due.

fields.label: Recording File
fields.description: OUR copy of the audio, owned by the call. A pointer, never the bytes — the File row is the one authority on name, privacy and where it really lives.

fields.label: Recording Source
fields.description: Who produced the audio. Stamped onto the stored file's name so the producer is readable at a glance in the container and on the Files tab.

fields.label: Producer's URL
fields.description: Where the producer published the audio — kept ONLY so a failed fetch can be retried, and never served. Playback is stored-or-nothing: if the bytes are not ours the screen says so rather than pointing a patient's audio at somebody else's host.

fields.label: Fetch Attempts
fields.description: How many times the bytes have been asked for. What turns an Awaiting row into an Abandoned one instead of retrying for ever.

fields.label: Next Attempt At
fields.description: When the sweep may try again. Backoff, so a producer having a bad hour is not hammered once a minute.

fields.label: Last Fetch Error
fields.description: Why the last attempt failed, in the producer's own words. An operator reading an Abandoned row has the reason on the row rather than in a log search.
